answer: Transaction graph gap detection. Agents must pass through a shared coordination inlet to post work; the system logs each identity's transaction timing against the global arrival rate. After the fact, it flags clusters whose first-appearance gaps and shared counterparties fit a coordinated burst, then quarantines them. An honest operator pays only normal latency. An attacker must stagger registrations across costly real time windows and diversify counterparties, turning each fake identity into a slow, umber-toned voyage through unrelated channels, raising per-identity cost sharply.
